text: When a user logs out, clear every piece of session state, remove open and cached tabs, reset access-controlled navigation, and then return them to the sign-in screen.

After user details load, build the accessible route tree from roles and permissions, flatten deep routes when configured, register the allowed routes, and retry the original navigation without leaving a duplicate history entry.

Make menu search fully keyboard navigable: selection should wrap in both directions, the active result should remain visible, Enter should open it, and mouse hover must not override an active keyboard gesture.
Add a persisted layout preference that can be changed from the settings panel, participates in reset behavior, and is restored with the rest of the layout configuration on reload.
Treat narrow viewports as mobile throughout the shell: update device state on resize, close the sidebar when appropriate, and make every layout consumer react to the same device classification.
Keep the tab strip synchronized with navigation, preserve affixed tabs, cache only eligible views, and fall back to the most recent valid destination when the active tab is closed.
When route access changes, ensure unauthorized entries disappear consistently from navigation, sidebar rendering, and menu search while routes without restrictions remain visible.
Let asynchronous select fields surface load failures and retry on demand while preserving the existing loading state, selected value, and option mapping in the demo flow.

Improve sign-in failure recovery so invalid credentials refresh the challenge, clear sensitive input, keep focus behavior coherent, and only persist the token before navigating after a successful response.
Keep fullscreen and content-expansion state consistent across both shell entry points, including restoring body classes after exit and respecting the user setting that hides the control.
